verses.english: Linked Discourses 36.21
3. The Explanation of the Hundred and Eight
With Sīvaka

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

verses.pali: Atha kho moḷiyasīvako paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
verses.english: Then the wanderer Moḷiyasīvaka went up to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

verses.pali: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho moḷiyasīvako paribbājako bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

verses.pali: “santi, bho gotama, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṁvādino evaṁdiṭṭhino:
verses.english: “Worthy Gotama, there are some ascetics and brahmins who have this doctrine and view:

verses.pali: ‘yaṁ kiñcāyaṁ purisapuggalo paṭisaṁvedeti sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā sabbaṁ taṁ pubbekatahetū’ti.
verses.english: ‘Everything this individual person experiences—pleasurable, painful, or neutral—is because of past deeds.’
What does the worthy Gotama say about this?”
“Sīvaka, some feelings stem from bile disorders.

verses.pali: Sāmampi kho etaṁ, sīvaka, veditabbaṁ yathā pittasamuṭṭhānānipi idhekaccāni vedayitāni uppajjanti.
verses.english: You can know this from your own personal experience,

verses.pali: Lokassapi kho etaṁ, sīvaka, saccasammataṁ yathā pittasamuṭṭhānānipi idhekaccāni vedayitāni uppajjanti.
verses.english: and it is generally deemed to be true.

verses.pali: Tatra, sīvaka, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṁvādino evaṁdiṭṭhino:
verses.english: Since this is so, the ascetics and brahmins whose view is that

verses.pali: ‘yaṁ kiñcāyaṁ purisapuggalo paṭisaṁvedeti sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā sabbaṁ taṁ pubbekatahetū’ti.
verses.english: everything an individual person experiences is because of past deeds

verses.pali: Yañca sāmaṁ ñātaṁ tañca atidhāvanti, yañca loke saccasammataṁ tañca atidhāvanti.
verses.english: go beyond personal experience and beyond what is generally deemed to be true.
So those ascetics and brahmins are wrong, I say.
Some feelings stem from phlegm disorders …
wind disorders …
their conjunction …
change in weather …
not taking care of yourself …
overexertion …

verses.pali: kammavipākajānipi kho, sīvaka, idhekaccāni vedayitāni uppajjanti.
verses.english: Some feelings are the result of past deeds.
You can know this from your own personal experience,
and it is generally deemed to be true.

verses.pali: tatra, sīvaka, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṁvādino evaṁdiṭṭhino:
verses.english: Since this is so, the ascetics and brahmins whose view is that

verses.pali: ‘yaṁ kiñcāyaṁ purisapuggalo paṭisaṁvedeti sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā sabbaṁ taṁ pubbekatahetū’ti.
verses.english: everything an individual person experiences is because of past deeds

verses.pali: Yañca sāmaṁ ñātaṁ tañca atidhāvanti yañca loke saccasammataṁ tañca atidhāvanti.
verses.english: go beyond personal experience and beyond what is generally deemed to be true.
So those ascetics and brahmins are wrong, I say.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, moḷiyasīvako paribbājako bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When he said this, the wanderer Moḷiyasīvaka said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent! …

verses.pali: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
verses.english: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
“Bile, phlegm, and wind,
their conjunction, and the weather,
not taking care of yourself, overexertion,
and the result of deeds is the eighth.”
